messages.author: ada06c1231306478
messages.subject: Issue with groupComparison function
parts:
Hi,

I am working with DIA-PASEF data that I ran through Fragpipe.  I have 4 conditions (Double_negative, FASN, PCK1, Double_positive) based on cells sorted with PrimeFlow.  I have set up the following comparison matrix and run groupComparison to determine what is different between all of the conditions:

#comparision test
comparison1 <- matrix(c(1,-1,0,0), nrow = 1)
comparison2 <- matrix(c(1,0,-1,0), nrow = 1)
comparison3 <- matrix(c(1,0,0,-1), nrow = 1)
comparison4 <- matrix(c(0,1,-1,0), nrow = 1)
comparison5 <- matrix(c(0,1,0,-1), nrow = 1)
comparison6 <- matrix(c(0,0,1,-1), nrow = 1)

comparison <- rbind(comparison1, comparison2, comparison3, comparison4, comparison5, comparison6)

row.names(comparison) <- c("Double_negative-FASN", "Double_negative-PCK1", "Double_negative-Double_positive",
                           "FASN-PCK1", "FASN-Double_positive", "PCK1-Double_positive")
colnames(comparison) <- c("Double_negative", "FASN", "PCK1", "Double_positive")

#run comparison function
group_comparison <- groupComparison(comparison, processed_data)

However, when I go to run groupComparisonPlots, I get the following error:

When I make a df of group_comparison$ComparisonResult, I get a df where log2FC is either a +/- number, -Inf, or Inf.  Also in the df, SE, Tvalue, DF, pvalue, adj.pvalue are either NaN or NA.  I see these two results throughout the whole df and here is an example of what it looks like:

I understand that the groupComparisonPlots function probably should not work given the data that is stored in the output of groupComparison (in my case group_comparison) under ComparisonResult.  However, I am not sure what I did wrong leading up to this point that leads to the Infs and NAs.  In dataProcess, I left MBimpute = TRUE.

I have included a copy of my markdown file.  Let me know if you need anything else.

Thank you,
Max

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: Issue with groupComparison function
parts:
Posting rest of conversation that is not showing up here in case it helps someone else:

Hi Devon,

This is just a pilot experiment so I only have one replicate in each group.  There are 4 groups that I want to compare each group with each other group.

Best,
Max

----------

Hi Max,

This makes sense. You are getting fold changes but nothing else because you only have one replicate per group. It is impossible to estimate a variance with single replicate groups. We will still report the fold change between the singular replicates.

Devon
